recentItems.title: Los residentes se preparan ante la amenaza del huracán Polo en la costa suroeste de México
recentItems.description:
(23 Sep 2026) 
SUMARIO DE RESTRICCIONES:

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Acapulco, México - 22 de septiembre de 2026 
1. Plano general de la playa de Acapulco 
2. Oleaje llegando a la playa 
3. Olas rompiendo en la playa
4. Grupo de jóvenes practicando *skimboarding* en la playa 
5. SOUNDBITE (Español) Josefino Rivera, contador y surfista: 
++PARTES SUPERPUESTAS CON TOMAS 3,4++
"En este momento, el huracán Polo vino con muchísima fuerza, mucha intensidad. Categoría 5. Demasiada intensidad, si lo pueden observar hay olas como de 5 metros con corriente, corriente de retorno; esta demasiado peligroso".  
6. Camión de la Guardia Nacional circulando y alertando a la gente por llegada de huracán 
7. Diversas tomas de árboles meciéndose con el viento
8. El taxista Juan José García Viviano hablando con un colega junto a su taxi 
9. SOUNDBITE (Español) Juan José García Viviano, taxista: 
“Si que estamos realmente preocupados por lo que viene ahorita en este momento. Y aparece que las personas que viven en los arroyos, las que viven en los barrancos, hay que tener mas precaución. Hay que salirse de ese lugar para que no vaya a pasar algo mas, una desgracia en la familia”.

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Lázaro Cárdenas, México - 22 de septiembre de 2026  
1O. Pobladores llenando sacos de arena
11. Restaurantes a pie de playa bajo palmeras que se mecen 
12. SOUNDBITE (Español) Concepción López Villegas, profesora de cocina tradicional: 
++PARTES SUPERPUESTAS con Tomas 11, 13++ 
“Nosotros andamos preocupándonos por nuestros negocios, que estén protegidos, claro nos sentimos tristes porque este es nuestro patrimonio y que de la noche a la mañana se nos acabe este patrimonio”.
13. Olas rompiendo contra un restaurante protegido con sacos de arena 
STORYLINE:
El huracán Polo se ha convertido en una de las tormentas más potentes en décadas en el Pacífico y se espera que roce la costa suroeste de México como un huracán mayor, mientras que, también en el Pacífico, Odalys ganó fuerza el miércoles y alcanzó categoría de huracán pero no supone una amenaza en tierra firme.

El Centro Nacional de Huracanes de Estados Unidos en Miami (NHC, por sus siglas en inglés) calificó a Polo de tormenta “extremadamente peligrosa” y pronosticó que girará bruscamente hacia el noroeste antes de desplazarse hacia el oeste-noroeste durante los próximos días.

Polo puso de nuevo en alerta a los habitantes de la costa mexicana del Pacífico, tras haber sufrido el embate de potentes ciclones en varias ocasiones durante los últimos años. 

Las playas quedaron casi desiertas y nubes oscuras se arremolinaban sobre un mar agitado, mientras las autoridades mexicanas suspendían temporalmente las clases el martes en diversas zonas. 

En Acapulco, algunos jóvenes practicaban *skimboarding* a pesar de las advertencias sobre las peligrosas condiciones del mar. 

"El huracán Polo vino con muchísima fuerza, Demasiada intensidad", dijo el contador y surfista Josefino Rivera. 

El miércoles, el meteoro estaba a unos 266 kilómetros al sur de Zihuatanejo y a 515 kms al sureste de Manzanillo, y avanzaba en dirección norte con vientos máximos sostenidos de 241 km/h, según el NHC. 

Eso lo situaba cerca de la parte alta de la categoría 4, tras haber tenido anteriormente categoría 5.

Las autoridades suspendieron temporalmente las clases el martes en varias zonas. La Marina de México cerró puertos en los estados de Guerrero y Michoacán y advirtió a civiles y pescadores que extremaran las precauciones.

Concepción López Villegas se afanaba en preparar su restaurante junto al mar para lo que pudiera venir.

recentItems.title: Protesters demand full recognition of Kurdish language in schools in northern Syria
recentItems.description:
(23 Sep 2026) 
SYRIA KURDISH PROTEST 

SOURCE: ASSOCIATED PRESS

RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

LENGTH: 2:00

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Qamishli, Syria - 22 September 2026
1. Wide of students and people protesting in Qamishli with flags
2. Students chanting, UPSOUND (Kurdish): “There is no life without language”
3. Man beating on Middle Eastern drums, known as darbuka
4. Women beating on the Daf, another Middle Eastern drum, during the protest 
5. Kurdish flags in the city 
6. SOUNDBITE (Kurdish) Rojin Musa, 35-year-old teacher of Kurdish:
“It has been 15 years that we've taught our children in their own language. So, it is not right at all today to see another language being imposed, and our children are being prevented from learning in their own (native) language. Therefore, our message is to include the Kurdish language officially in the constitution's draft and be recognized as a people living on their own land.”

7. Wide of women protesters chanting UPSOUND (Kurdish): “Who are we? We are Kurds” and carrying a banner reading (Arabic/Kurdish): “Our language, our constitutional right"
8. Close of woman protesting
9. Protesters holding banners and chanting (Kurdish): “There is no life without language”
10. Various of the protest, music in the background
11. Student holding sign reading (Kurdish): “Our language is our identity”
12. SOUNDBITE (Kurdish) Bashir Badli, 46-year-old father of three students:
“I have three children and they have been going to Kurdish schools for seven years. I mean they have been studying in Kurdish for seven years. They reached seventh, eighth, and final year school. Now, they have been told to study in another language. Therefore, we came out today to support our language, so our efforts and our children’s efforts are not wasted. Our language means our existence. Our language means our land. We are Kurds. We want the Kurdish language.”

13. Various of protest, protesters holding Kurdish flags and chanting
STORYLINE:
Hundreds of students and their families held a protest on Tuesday in the northeastern Syrian city of Qamishli over a government decree that makes Kurdish an official language of instruction in Syria, but only provides for three classes a week. 

In recent days, students have staged similar protests in the Kurdish majority-city, and Hassakeh.

Under the rule of former Syrian President Bashar Assad, the Kurdish language was banned in schools. 

But during the war, authorities affiliated with the Kurd-led Syrian Democratic Forces in the northeast set up a school system teaching mostly in Kurdish.

Bashir Badli, a 46-year-old father of three, said that his children have studied extensively in Kurdish for seven years. 

"Now, they have been told to study in another language," he explained, saying that learning in Arabic would be a hindrance to their education. 

"Our language means our existence. Our language means our land," he added. 

Rojin Musa, a 35-year-old teacher of Kurdish demanded that the language be officially codified in the Syrian constitution, and used as a language for instruction in schools. 

The protest was part of the latest discontent in the Kurdish region in the midst of a push to integrate the once-powerful Kurd-led force into Syria’s army and bring formerly autonomous institutions under the control of the central government.

The integration agreement with the Syrian Democratic Forces has been widely regarded as a victory for the government of interim President Ahmad al-Sharaa.




"We are Kurds. We want the Kurdish language" Badi said. 

AP video by Hogir El Abdo

recentItems.title: Saudi Arabia's airshow ushers in national day festivities
recentItems.description:
(23 Sep 2026) 
SAUDI ARABIA NATIONAL DAY AIRSHOW

SOURCE: ASSOCIATED PRESS

RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

LENGTH: 2:08

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Malham, Riyadh Province, Saudi Arabia -  22 September 2026
1. Various of aircrafts performing aerobatic maneuvers during airshow
2. SOUNDBITE (English) Shan Alyar, resident from India:
"(It) was really awesome. Compared to the previous years, they are organised very well, praise be to God. We are able.. we can see very closely the Saudi defense system and all the aircrafts taking off and the landing. Everything, praise be to God, this time we enjoyed."

3. Aircrafts performing aerobatic stunts during airshow
4. Various of airplane towing a banner that reads (Arabic): "Our glory lies in our determination"
5.  SOUNDBITE (English) Subhana Alyar, resident from India: 
"It was surprising. We didn't expect this much. We used to see this from far away. This was so close. We saw each and every aircraft individually, so it was a different experience."

6. Various of people holding Saudi flags during show
7. Various of Saudi Falcons aircrafts, in green and white
8. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Saud al-Bassam, resident: 
"It is amazing, praise be to God. I didn't expect such organization and magnificence."

9. Various of Saudi riders on horseback carrying national flags 
10. Military vehicle displayed
11. Aircraft performing aerobatic maneuvers with smoke trails
STORYLINE:
Dazzling air shows, military parades, and outdoor gatherings were the highlight of the airshow organized as part of the several events taking place across the country to celebrate Saudi Arabia's National Day. 

In Malham, in Riyadh province, military aircrafts roared overhead in formations of white and green on Tuesday while families watched, waving Saudi flags and taking pictures. 

On the ground, Saudi horse riders were seen carrying national flags throughout the celebration.

The display took place a day before the kingdom's 96th National Day on Sept. 23, commemorating the 1932 unification by founder King Abdul-Aziz Al Saud.

Originally from India but living in the country for years, Shan Alyar and her wife, Subhana Alyar, were among the spectators surprised for getting so close access to see the show. 

"(It) was really awesome," he said. "Compared to the previous years, they are organised very well."

Saudi resident Saud al-Bassam also enjoyed the festivities, lauding their organization.  

The event took place despite the tensions with Yemen and the threats of attacks from the Houthi rebels. 

AP video by Baraa Anwer

recentItems.title: Danish lawmakers welcome agreement between Denmark, Greenland, and US
recentItems.description:
(23 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY: 

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Copenhagen, Denmark - 23 September 2026
1. Christiansborg Palace parliament building exterior, pan left
2. Statue 
3. Various of Christiansborg Palace exterior
4. Various of Christiansborg Palace interior
5. Mid of Lars-Christian Brask, Danish lawmaker and member of government’s Foreign Policy Committee 
6. SOUNDBITE (English) Lars-Christian Brask, Danish lawmaker and member of government’s Foreign Policty Committee:
"You have to be a NATO member, or a NATO partner, or the US, or in the EU to basically come in with critical infrastructure. That's new. It is new that this agreement only holds as long as NATO holds together. Huge importance, because that basically means NATO has to hold together and because it is important for the US that they have the abilities with bases etc., in Greenland. And also that, if Greenland becomes independent it will still be an agreement that is in force. That's major changes from 1951 and 91 and 2004 updates."
7. Cutaway of Brask
8. SOUNDBITE (English) Lars-Christian Brask, Danish lawmaker and member of government's Foreign Policy Committee:
"I think this is a step in the right direction and things have to take time to heal and I'm sure it will also take time to heal here, but we've raised the level of trust, so we have a good platform to build on."
9. Various of Christiansborg Palace interior
10. SOUNDBITE (English) Lars-Christian Brask, Danish lawmaker and member of government's Foreign Policy Committee:
"It was a wake-up call, and it was wake-up call in the regard that you had to get out of bed. You couldn't put it on snooze and turn around. You had to react, for the interest of Greenland, for the interests of the Kingdom of Denmark."
11. Various of Christiansborg Palace interior
12. Various of Trine Pertou Mach, Danish lawmaker and member of government's Foreign Policy Committee
13. SOUNDBITE (English) Trine Pertou Mach, Danish lawmaker and member of government's Foreign Policy Committee:
"The agreement of yesterday is an agreement of 2026 and not 1951. The most obvious change is that Greenland is part of the agreement. They are signing it, they have been negotiating, they had a seat at the table. And that is absolutely crucial for me, that it's not about Greenland, it's with Greenland."
14. Various of Christiansborg Palace interior
15. SOUNDBITE (English) Trine Pertou Mach, Danish lawmaker and member of government's Foreign Policy Committee:
"It's been bloody damaging, and you have seen it in the polls. It's only a minority of Danes now having trust in the US as an ally and partner. So it will take a very long time to rebuild. So this agreement is not going to do away with that mistrust."
16. Various of Christiansborg Palace interior
17. SOUNDBITE (English) Trine Pertou Mach, Danish lawmaker and member of government's Foreign Policy Committee:
"We have a lot in our past that we need to unpack and get over jointly. And I think this agreement now, having Denmark and Greenland working basically hand in hand in and out of meetings, having a common cause and also a common result is really important for Greenland to be on its own, not just being part of what Denmark is doing."
18. Christiansborg Palace spire
19. Statue, Christiansborg Palace in background 
20. Christiansborg Palace, people passing by in foreground
21. Danish flag, Christiansborg Palace in background 
STORYLINE:
Danish lawmakers Lars-Christian Brask and Trine Pertou Mach on Wednesday welcomed the agreement signed between Denmark, Greenland and the US.











AP video by James Brooks

recentItems.title: Leader of Morocco's opposition PPS arrives to vote in parliamentary election
recentItems.description:
(23 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Rabat, Morocco - 23 September 2026
1.⁠ ⁠Mohamed Nabil Benabdallah, General Secretary of the Progress and Socialism Party (PPS) arriving at the polling station with his wife 
2.⁠ Media filming Mohamed Nabil Benabdallah
3.⁠ ⁠Benabdallah talking to clerks at voting office
4.⁠ ⁠SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Mohamed Nabil Benabdallah, General Secretary, Progress and Socialism Party (PPS):
"Like all the Moroccan citizens, I did my duty in Rabat. I am optimistic and wishing the best for this process. We hope that the results will reflect the expectations of the citizens at all levels. I hope that the process will go on in the best way possible until the counting of the votes and the announcement of the results.”
5. Various of registered voter lists at polling station
STORYLINE:
The leader of Morocco's opposition PPS (Party of Progress and Socialism) arrived at a polling station in Rabat on Wednesday to vote in the parliamentary election.

Mohamed Nabil Benabdallah said he was "optimistic and wishing the best for this process," after casting his ballot.  

"We hope that the results will reflect the expectations of the citizens at all levels,” he added. 

Moroccan voters were choosing a new parliament Wednesday in an election shaped by mounting frustration among young people, high unemployment despite a thriving economy, and demands for better schools, hospitals and housing.

Voting centers across the North African kingdom have been open from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time, allowing nearly 16 million registered voters to cast ballots for the 395-seat House of Representatives.

The election will be the first since deadly youth-led protests nearly a year ago and a mass attempt by migrants to cross Morocco’s northern border into the Spanish territory of Ceuta that left dozens dead.

The next government will oversee billions of dollars in investment as Morocco prepares to co-host the 2030 FIFA World Cup, prompting some to describe it as the “World Cup government.”

The new political leadership will also face pressure to address everyday concerns, including jobs, wages and the cost of living.

Voters will choose among 7,288 candidates from 27 political parties.

"I hope that the process will go on in the best way possible until the counting of the votes and the announcement of the results,” said Benabdallah.

STORYLINE:
Russia hammered Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, with drones in daylight attacks on Wednesday, hours before Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy was due to address world leaders at the U.N. General Assembly.

Two people were killed and 23 were wounded in Kyiv, and palls of black smoke floated above the city following the latest in what have been daily Russian attacks that torment Ukrainian civilians. 

The drones set off fires and damaged buildings in Kyiv and elsewhere in Ukraine overnight, according to authorities.

recentItems.title: UN and Interpol officials at Cambodia conference highlight challenges of cyberscam crackdowns
recentItems.description:
(23 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Chrey Thum, Kandal Province, Cambodia -  22 September 2026
1. Various of abandoned casino within closed Jin Wan scam compound in Cambodia
2. Various of abandoned computer equipment and cables in compound

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Phnom Penh, Cambodia - 23 September 2026
3. Wide of Delphine Schantz, Regional Representative of United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) Regional Office for Southeast Asia and the Pacific speaking
4. SOUNDBITE (English) Delphine Schantz, Regional Representative, United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) Regional Office for Southeast Asia and the Pacific (ROSEAP): 
"Southeast Asia is a region of rapid digitalization, but even here, criminals have outpaced most other sectors of the society. We see this in the growing global reach of scam centers, but we also see this in the rapid expansion of other online crime types, like illegal gambling, or the distribution of malware."

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Kamchay Mear district, Prey Veng Province, Cambodia - 21 September 2026
5. Abandoned working area at "No.8 Park", a huge scam compound run by Chinese tycoon Chen Zhi who was arrested in January and accused of running scam operation, shot during media tour
6. Discarded mattresses
7. Computer monitors

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Phnom Penh, Cambodia - 23 September 2026
8. Wide of Nicholas Court, Director of Taskforce Coordination Directorate of International Criminal Police Organization speaking
9. SOUNDBITE (English) Nicholas Court, Director of Taskforce Coordination Directorate, International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol):
"Scam centers, especially in this region, are increasingly being moved from large centers into much smaller ones, which are harder to trace. But what that tells us is that law enforcement efforts are having an impact here. However, fraud remains the most significant crime type by volume in the world. The most recent estimate from the global anti-scam alliances that more than 440 billion US dollars are lost to fraud every year."

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Kamchay Mear district, Prey Veng Province, Cambodia - 21 September 2026
10. Abandoned working areas in scam compound ++NIGHT SHOTS++

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Phnom Penh, Cambodia - 23 September 2026
11. SOUNDBITE (English) Delphine Schantz, Regional Representative, United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) Regional Office for Southeast Asia and the Pacific (ROSEAP): 
"More can be done and needs to be done at the national levels, but also at the regional and international level, and in terms of international cooperation. More than ever, the saying is true that it is not a matter that any country can resolve on its own."

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Chrey Thum, Kandal Province, Cambodia -  22 September 2026
12. Exterior of Jin Wan scam compound
13. Various of abandoned scooters at Jin Wan scam compound
STORYLINE:
Officials from the United Nations office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and Interpol warned of the multi-faceted and growing threat of cyber scams in Southeast Asia despite recent crackdowns, while speaking at a conference in Cambodia on Wednesday.

Experts speaking at the conference in Phnom Penh applauded Cambodia's efforts, but highlighted ongoing issues.

Cambodia hosted the two-day conference with the U.N. Office on Drugs and Crime and Interpol. It took reporters to a few empty scam compounds on Monday and Tuesday to showcase its efforts to close them.


In her remarks, Schantz acknowledged the shared responsibility of strengthening the crackdown on cyber crime and the importance of international coordination.

recentItems.title: Greenland deal between Denmark and US a 'win for all three parties', analyst says
recentItems.description:
(23 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Copenhagen, Denmark - 23 September 2026
1. Set up shots of Marc Jacobsen, associate professor at the Royal Danish Defence College and head of research at Center for Arctic Security Studies, speaking during interview
2. SOUNDBITE (English) Marc Jacobsen, associate professor at the Royal Danish Defence College and head of research at the Center for Arctic Security Studies:
"Well, it's a win for all three parties. I think, for Donald Trump, it is a win because he has to close this. He has a lot of things going on. He has a trade war with Canada. He has a very unpopular war in Iran. So it's important for him to close this and appear, at least, as a winner. So he's praised in the Republican-friendly media and by his close people and his political circles as a winner, as a good negotiator that he actually achieved something new."
3. Cutaway of Marc speaking 
4. SOUNDBITE (English) Marc Jacobsen, associate professor at the Royal Danish Defence College and head of research at Center for Arctic Security Studies:
"It's interesting that it isn't that different from the present agreement from 1951, which was updated in 2004. I think there are three concrete new things. One thing is that it's more concrete on who are welcome and, thereby, who are not welcome. So it's NATO member states, NATO partners, EU members. And then the ones who not welcome to, for instance, have military presence or invest in Greenland, they are all the others, but it's mainly about Russia and China, certainly."
5. Cutaway 
6. SOUNDBITE (English) Marc Jacobsen, associate professor at the Royal Danish Defence College and head of research at Center for Arctic Security Studies:
"This agreement is an important achievement, and it hopefully settles these weekly intimidations from Donald Trump against the Greenlanders. But of course it has been going on for almost two years now. So, the level of trust is very low in comparison with two years ago. So in Denmark and Greenland there's kind of post-traumatic stress now. So you have to, of course, rebuild this relationship."
7. Cutaway to of church
8. SOUNDBITE (English) Marc Jacobsen, associate professor at the Royal Danish Defence College and head of research at Center for Arctic Security Studies:
"This whole episode has, of course, Greenland would have liked it not to happen, but still it enhances Greenland's international agency. So other states are more inclined to call directly to Nuuk instead of Copenhagen. We saw yesterday at the press meeting that the Prime Minister, the Premier of Greenland, he shined; he really took the international stage. So I think maybe Greenland will not become independent within the next few years. But in the meantime, it can increase its self-determination, and part of that is to at least appear as a more autonomous foreign policy actor."
9. Pan left of Marc speaking
STORYLINE:
President Donald Trump on Tuesday signed an agreement with Denmark and Greenland aimed at strengthening Arctic and North Atlantic security, paving the way for more U.S. bases in Greenland and easing tensions over his repeated calls for the vast island to become part of the United States. 


According to analysts, the agreement is a win for all the parties involved. 


The signing on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York comes days after Trump announced the deal to bolster the U.S. military presence in Greenland but keep it under Danish control.

Marc further explained the details of the agreement and the members actively involved in it.

17. SOUNDBITE (French) Catherine Vautrin, French Minister of the Armed Forces and Veterans: ++QUALITY AS INCOMING++
"I emphasize this word, partnership - because today we have two sovereign countries who effectively wish to work together, because working together means allowing interoperability between our two armed forces." 
18. Vautrin and Sjamsoeddin shaking hands
19. Vautrin and Sjamsoeddin walking away
STORYLINE:
The French Minister of the Armed Forces and Veterans, Catherine Vautrin, met with her Indonesian counterpart on Wednesday in Jakarta to reaffirm the strengthening of defense and military-industrial cooperation between the two countries.

Indonesian Defense Minister Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin said in a statement that Indonesian National Armed Forces troops will conduct the Garuda Guerrier joint exercise with the French military in France next November.

This meeting also marks the first Annual French-Indonesian Industrial Dialogue between the two countries.

“We hope this will serve as a pivotal moment in strengthening not only defense cooperation, but also cooperation between the people of Indonesia and France,” Sjamsoeddin said on Wednesday.

Military cooperation between Indonesia and France has grown in recent years, since President Prabowo Subianto was still serving as Indonesia’s defense minister.

In 2024, Indonesia purchased 42 Rafale and Dassault Aviation fighter jets. 

It also announced the purchase of two French Scorpene Evolved submarines and 13 Thales Ground Control Interception radars. Five of the radar systems are expected to be installed in the country’s new capital, Nusantara.

Sjamsoeddin added that Indonesia appreciates the strengthening of cooperation in the field of defense equipment, as marked by the arrival of the first Rafale in Indonesia this year and the start of construction of the first Scorpene submarine by state-owned shipbuilder PT PAL Indonesia.
